who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code
what: The one build queue stood still for 22 minutes with five lanes waiting and the VM idle: `lslocks` showed `/root/loop.lock` held by `blaze-engine serve`, a daemon started by an earlier loop command. Two lanes reported it and both named the wrong holder (the first waiter); I ended that waiter's `flock`, which made it build without the lock until I stopped it.
cost: 22 minutes for five lanes; one build started outside the lock
cause: the lock was `exec 9>lock; flock 9`, and every child inherited descriptor 9; a daemon outlives the command that started it
whys: why stuck: a daemon held the lock
why possible: the lock is a property of an open descriptor and children inherit descriptors
why not caught: nothing said who held the lock; waiters looked the same as the holder in `ps`
why easy: the shell idiom for a lock is inheritable by default
property: a resource meant for one scope is held by whatever outlives that scope
class: scope leak: a lock, pipe, descriptor or lease taken for one command is inherited by a process that outlives it (the same class as a daemon holding a caller's stdout pipe open, which also happened in that script)
prevention: loop.sh starts every child with the lock closed (9>&-), sends a command's output to a file and prints it after, stops a command at 600 s, and says who holds the lock; a watchdog ends a stray holder. Open: blaze's own daemon closes every descriptor it did not ask for when it starts (CLOEXEC by default, close_range at spawn), with a test that a daemon started from a process holding a lock does not hold it
fix: loop.sh fixed 2026-11-12; the daemon-side close is open
